artifacts.summary: Confirms exactly two scope-excursion emitters (git-commit-phase.sh, git-commit-scoped.sh); recommends emitter-side collapse via a shared library function reusing issue-log.md's already-documented but never-consumed tags.occurrence convention, extended with a full tags.dropped_paths array for no-suppression; finds zero changes needed to issue-record.sh or orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh; corrects the dispatch's Verification reference from issue-grouping.sh (unrelated /review tooling) to orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh's own group_by pipeline; flags a doc/code asymmetry in git-staging-scope.md regarding a third, non-recording site.

memory_candidates.content: issue-log.md's Occurrence Collapse convention (tags.occurrence = {count, first_seen, last_seen} via --tags-json) was fully documented, with scope-excursion named as its intended use case, but had zero real callers anywhere in the codebase until this task. tags is validated by issue-record.sh only as type==object (no interior-shape checks), so adding a sibling key like tags.dropped_paths is never a schema change -- a write-side collapse of N per-path issue rows into one record needs no change to issue-record.sh or to orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh's group_by(.class) pipeline, which already groups by JSONL line regardless of path count. When a caller already knows its full repeat count before its first issue-record.sh call, prefer this existing seam over inventing a new one.

issue-grouping.sh and tier-selection.sh implement the /review command's own issue-triage pipeline (schema: source/file_path/severity critical-high-medium-low) and are NOT consumers of issues.jsonl (issue-record.sh's schema: kind/class/severity blocking-costly-minor-none). A task description or dispatch naming issue-grouping.sh as a consumer of issues.jsonl rows is factually wrong -- the actual read-time consumer to check against is orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh's own group_by(.class) pipeline.

git-commit-phase.sh and git-commit-scoped.sh already share small per-concern library files (lib/engine-written-state-paths-lib.sh, lib/derived-artifact-probe-lib.sh) sourced independently by both scripts rather than duplicating logic. This is the established precedent to reuse whenever a new piece of shared call-construction logic (e.g. a batched issue-record.sh wrapper) needs to live beside these two scripts' per-script loop/accumulation code without duplicating the shared part twice.
